scenes.heading: Constraints
scenes.subheading: Rules that keep your data valid
scenes.narration: Constraints are rules you attach to a table so the database automatically enforces the correctness of your data.

scenes.heading: Common constraint types
bullets: NOT NULL requires a value to be present
PRIMARY KEY combines unique and not-null
CHECK validates values against a condition
scenes.narration: A NOT NULL constraint requires that a column always has a value. A UNIQUE constraint forbids duplicate values in a column. A PRIMARY KEY constraint combines uniqueness and not-null to give each row identity. A FOREIGN KEY constraint ensures references point to rows that exist, and a CHECK constraint validates values against a condition you define.

scenes.heading: Applying constraints in SQL
scenes.narration: This table layers several constraints to protect its data. The name column cannot be null, the price must be zero or positive thanks to the CHECK, and the sku must be unique across all rows. Because the database enforces these rules on every insert and update, invalid data can never sneak in. Constraints therefore move data validation from application code into the database itself.

scenes.text: Constraints let the database enforce correctness automatically, so bad data never gets in.
scenes.narration: The key idea is that constraints push correctness into the database, guaranteeing that invalid data can never be stored in the first place.
